No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result ‘I’ve Tried To Make Peace For 40 Years’ — Okoya’s Son Begs Billionaire Father For Forgiveness by Nafisat Abdulrahman 11 seconds ago in News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram Fatai Okoya, who identifies himself as the first child of billionaire businessman Razaq Okoya, has appealed to his father for forgiveness after about 40 years of estrangement, blaming their strained relationship on a money dispute and his decision to marry a woman his father reportedly disapproved of.
Fatai appealed during a TikTok Live session with blogger Yeye Kudi Court Room on Monday, where he recounted his unsuccessful attempts to reconcile with the founder of Eleganza Group and his disappointment over an alleged encounter at the businessman’s 86th birthday celebration.
According to him, the disagreement began when he was younger, after he took a small amount of money from his father’s company, and he insisted that the incident did not warrant decades of separation.
“I did not embezzle much money; if it was much, I would have built a house and bought planes and cars,” he said in Yoruba.
Fatai also attributed the rift to his decision to marry a woman his father did not approve of, explaining that he was young and in love at the time.
He said he had spent decades trying to mend their relationship but had yet to secure a reunion with his father.
Recounting his experience at Razaq Okoya’s 86th birthday celebration, Fatai alleged that he was initially welcomed at the event but was later prevented from approaching his father.
He said he was informed that his father had to be notified before he could meet him.
“But my father did not have anything to say. So I had to turn back and go and sit down in my chair,” he said.
Fatai maintained that his appeal was not driven by financial considerations but by his desire to restore his relationship with his father and reconnect with the family.
He further alleged that he had made several attempts to reach the businessman through friends and intermediaries but had been unable to arrange a meeting.
Fatai’s daughter, identified as Zee during the live session, also appealed for a reconciliation, saying she had no relationship with her grandfather and wanted to help her father reconnect with him.
She said she knew her father missed his father after spending years apart.
The host also called on people close to the billionaire businessman to intervene and help resolve the family dispute, specifically appealing to Chief Kesington Adebutu, popularly known as Baba Ijebu, a friend of Razaq Okoya, to facilitate a reunion.
Renewing his plea, Fatai asked his father to forgive his past mistakes and give their relationship another chance.
“I’m begging my father. To err is human, to forgive is divine. He should, please, overlook all my behaviour as a child. He should please see that I, too, am a grown man. He should use his elderly wisdom to embrace us and bring us back to the family so that the issue can be settled once and for all,” he said.
Fatai added that he and his father had shared a close relationship while he was growing up, noting that he was the only child his mother had with the businessman.
